title: Function Lexicon
subtitle: Say it exactly — one sloppy word and the definition breaks.
description: A word game for the language of functions: hunt the wrong word, match terms to definitions, and prove which phrasings really mean the same thing.

rounds.prompt: Every function is a relation, but not every relation is a function.
rounds.explain: Functions are the relations with the one-output rule attached.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! A relation is any pairing of inputs and outputs. It only earns the name function when each input has exactly one output.

rounds.prompt: One word breaks this definition. Tap it.
rounds.sentence: A relation is a function when every input has exactly two outputs.
rounds.hint: Count the outputs a single input is allowed to have.
rounds.explain: Exactly one output per input — that is the whole rule.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! The broken word is two. A function gives each input exactly one output.

rounds.prompt: Which term names the set of all allowed inputs of $f$?
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! Range is the output set. Inputs live in the domain.

rounds.prompt: Connect each term to the definition it owns.

pairs.right: A line the graph races toward but never touches
Outputs rise as inputs move right

rounds.missExplain: Almost — read each definition for the words that give it away: $f(x) = 0$ means a zero, and outputs means range.

rounds.prompt: Select EVERY statement that says the same thing as $f(3) = 0$.
rounds.explain: Zero of $f$, $x$-intercept, and the point $(3, 0)$ are three names for one fact.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! Input 3 gives output 0, so 3 is a zero and $(3, 0)$ is on the graph. The $y$-axis and the range describe outputs, not this input.

rounds.prompt: Fill the missing term: the ______ of a function is the set of all its outputs.
rounds.missExplain: Almost — inputs are the domain, outputs are the range.

rounds.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it.
rounds.sentence: A one-to-one function passes the vertical line test, so it has an inverse function.
rounds.hint: Which test decides one-to-one, and which one decides function?
rounds.explain: Vertical test says function. Horizontal test says one-to-one, which is what buys you an inverse.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! Every function passes the vertical line test. It is the horizontal line test that proves one-to-one.

rounds.prompt: Sort each word by what it describes.
rounds.explain: You choose the input, the function decides the output.
rounds.missExplain: Almost — the independent variable is the $x$ you pick. Everything named $f(x)$ is what comes back out.

rounds.prompt: Three of these mean the same thing. Which one is the odd one out?
rounds.explain: Zeros, roots, and $x$-intercepts are one idea in three costumes.
rounds.missExplain: Trap sprung! The $y$-intercept is $f(0)$ — an output. The other three all describe an input that makes the output zero.
